research_question: When the environment changes, does warm-starting the population from the previous planning episode reduce replanning latency or improve solution quality compared with cold-start NSGA-II under the same objective-evaluation budget?

limitations: The fixed witness trajectory remains infeasible at every event; the schedule is a bounded clearance and violation stress case, not a feasibility-transition case.
The obstacle follows deterministic piecewise-linear motion and holds at its final waypoint after t=10.0.
This single scenario supports conclusions only about this schedule and these optimizer settings.

run_order: Alternate condition order by paired-seed index: cold then warm for even indices, warm then cold for odd indices.

metrics.objective_normalization_source: Fixed before the controlled run: path length scaled by the 125-unit bounded-world control-polygon ceiling, clearance risk by its [0,1] range, and log snap by a fixed 50-unit scale.
metrics.hypervolume_convention: Minimization hypervolume in fixed scaled objective space; points outside the frozen reference point are excluded by the existing metric implementation.
metrics.igd_convention: Euclidean IGD in the same fixed scaled objective space against the pooled feasible nondominated final-population front for the same event across both conditions and all paired seeds.
metrics.no_feasible_solution: Hypervolume is 0.0; IGD and feasible-only metrics are null when the event has no common feasible reference front or the run has no feasible solution.
metrics.multiple_comparison_correction: Holm correction across all event-by-metric tests separately for each paired-test family.
